messages:
deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout: redispatch-service v2.4.1 -> eu-west-1 (canary 10/100) — build 2026-03-15_18:00 :rocket:

matt: seeing a spike in 5xxs for redispatch in grafana. canary only but error rate jumped to ~8% in the last 2 minutes.

laura (SRE): paging when? looks like the canary hosts are failing decryption calls to KMS in the logs. attaching snippet.

matt: paste of the log: ```
2026-03-15T18:02:12Z ERROR redispatch.handler request_id=abc123 KMSDecryptionError: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/deploy-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
```

incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: S2 - redispatch canary failures in eu-west-1. Incident channel: #incidents. Paging on-call.

sara (oncall): I'm on it, looking at KMS permissions and recent key rotations. Any deploy config changes in this rollout?

matt: only change was v2 routing behavior + a small env var refactor. nothing KMS-related in code.

laura (SRE): checked KMS key alias timeline — key alias alias/redwood-deploy-eu was rotated yesterday by a scheduled rotation job at 02:12 UTC and the key policy was tightened (it looks like the deploy-role ARN was removed from the key policy). see audit event: `kms:UpdateKeyPolicy` by infra-bot.

sara (oncall): that would explain decrypt failures. canary instances can't read encrypted secrets (AWS creds used for downstream calls). assessing customer impact: current 5xx spike only in eu-west-1 canary subset — ~12 minutes duration so far. broad traffic unaffected for now.

ben: tagging customers? which tenants hit the canary?

matt: canary is 10% of eu-west traffic routed by canary router; traffic includes a handful of larger customers in EU staging — none in prod yet (we limit by account id). earliest ETA to kill the canary?

sara (oncall): attempting kill-switch (feature flag) to route traffic back to v1 immediately. toggling flag `use-v2-routing` -> false via flags API.

sara (oncall): `curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/api/flags/use-v2-routing -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -d '{"enabled":false}'`

ops-bot: FLAG-TOGGLE: use-v2-routing set to false by sara at 2026-03-15T18:06:48Z

matt: flag flip reported success, but dashboards not reflecting drop in errors — still seeing 5xx on canary hosts.

laura (SRE): looks like the flag toggle worked at the router level but some background worker processes still using v2 image due to in-flight sessions and cached routing. we should rollback the canary deploy to be safe.

sara (oncall): initiating rollback of the canary to v2.3.0 (previous stable).

sara (oncall): `deployctl rollback --service redispatch-service --to 2.3.0 --region eu-west-1 --canary-only`

deploy-bot: Rollback started: redispatch-service -> 2.3.0 (eu-west-1 canary).

matt: rolling logs show new instances coming up and joining, error rate dropping.

laura (SRE): confirm the root cause: key rotation removed deploy-role from KMS key policy — we need a follow-up to ensure scheduled rotations maintain deploy-role permission. For immediate mitigation we can re-add deploy-role to key policy or decrypt secrets and re-provision as plaintext to canary (short-term). Which do we prefer?

sara (oncall): re-applying policy change needs approval and could take time. quicker: redeploy with env var override using decrypted secret from ops account and then rotate the key policy back in a controlled window. but we need approval from infra/infosec. tagging infra.

ben: infra, can you confirm if restoring deploy-role to key policy is ok? @infra-team

incidents-bot: Paging infra-team on-call.

laura (SRE): also verifying whether any permanent secrets were exposed if we decrypt and re-inject — we will keep it in-memory on instances only, no logs.

infra (via ops-bot): restoring deploy-role to KMS policy is approved for emergency rollback. Doing `PutKeyPolicy` now.

ops-bot: AWS-KMS: PutKeyPolicy executed for key/abcd-ef01 by infra at 2026-03-15T18:12:03Z

deploy-bot: KMS decrypts succeeding on new canary instances. healthchecks green. error rate back to baseline (~0.2%).

sara (oncall): confirming service restored in eu-west canary. rolling back complete. marking incident as mitigated.

incidents-bot: Incident updated: mitigated. Time to mitigate ~12 minutes. Severity downgraded.

matt: customers impacted estimate: small percentage of EU canary traffic (~10% of eu-west region) for ~12 minutes; approximately 0.5% of total production requests. No billing or data leak indicators.

sara (oncall): handing off to ben for postmortem and follow-up. ben is now on-call for incident follow-up. :handshake:

ben: taking handoff. I will draft a postmortem and coordinate with infra/infosec to update rotation automation. immediate action items I see: [1] add deploy-role back into key rotation policy template, [2] add a post-rotation automated RBAC check that validates decrypt on a canary instance, [3] add a runbook step to kill canary and rollback if KMS decrypt fails.

laura (SRE): also recommend adding an alert rule for spikes in KMS Decryption errors aggregated across canary hosts (low false positive threshold).

ben: noted. I'll open a postmortem doc and link below.

matt: thanks all. small win that kill-switch + rollback path worked.

incidents-bot: Next steps assigned: ben -> postmortem (P0 for follow-up), infra -> update rotation template, sde -> add RBAC decrypt check in deploy pipeline.

sara (oncall): closing the pager. I'll stay in channel for questions for 30m.

ben: drafting postmortem: https://redwood-internal.docs/postmortems/redispatch-kms-rotation-1847520000 (placeholder)

laura (SRE): follow-up: schedule meeting with infosec to review key policy hardening + emergency allowances.

matt: thanks, closing thread. :white_check_mark:
